rounds.text: Hirect Ltd is backed by a rules-based screen scoring 75 out of 100 with a BUY rating, driven by strong top-line catalysts including a compounded sales growth of 42% over the trailing twelve months and recent quarterly profit growth [E14, E57, E60]. The fundamental engine operates with high capital efficiency, demonstrated by a robust return on equity of 25.2% and a return on capital employed of 18.8%, both outperforming broader sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E13]. Operational execution is further highlighted by a strong cash conversion of 2.21x against reported profit in March 2026, meaning profits are fully backed by cash with operating cash flow hitting Rs 86 Cr [E26, E27]. Institutional confidence is accelerating visibly, with foreign institutions lifting holdings to 6.84% and domestic institutions surging to 3.22%, generating a positive institutional money flow signal [E35, E36, E37]. This fundamental momentum rides squarely inside a supportive macro environment, given that the Capital Goods sector is experiencing a clear tailwind with a score of +1.04 [E65, E67]. Conceded: [E38] and [E39], which show a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 205 per share against a market price of Rs 1212, leaving a negative margin of safety.

Hirect Ltd is currently trading at a significant valuation premium that is disconnected from its underlying financial performance, with a P/E ratio of 134.1x compared to a sector benchmark of 23.87x [E6]. This extreme pricing is further highlighted by a price-to-book ratio of 19.97x [E2] and a reverse DCF analysis suggesting the market is pricing in 34.9% earnings growth, far exceeding the 10% base case assumption [E40]. While sales have grown, compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has actually declined by 9% [E15], and operating margins have compressed significantly, falling from 11% to 5% in the most recent quarter [E23]. Furthermore, the company’s financial health is pressured by rising debt, which has increased to Rs 245 Cr from Rs 164 Cr in the prior year, resulting in a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.17x [E30, E32]. The stock also carries substantial risk, evidenced by a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -79.8% and high annualised volatility of 53.3% [E46, E47]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong return on equity of 25.2% [E13] and has demonstrated positive institutional money flow [E37]. Despite these positive metrics, the current market price implies a margin of safety of -490.0% based on discounted cash flow projections [E39].

While the bear highlights a high P/E of 134.1x, it ignores that the stock's rules-based screen scores a solid 75 out of 100 on the strength of robust top-line momentum, featuring a compounded sales growth of 42% over the trailing twelve months and strong sales growth flagged by the screen [E14, E57, E59]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months reads -9% and quarterly operating margins compressed in the most recent period [E15, E23], but this is offset by accelerating earnings growth, a positive upcoming quarter expectation, and a high relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E44, E52, E61]. Although the bear points to rising borrowings of Rs 245 Cr and a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.17x [E30, E32], the company's working capital requirements have actually improved from 21.3 days to 14.9 days, and cash conversion reads an impressive 2.21x with profits fully backed by cash [E26, E53]. Conceded: the reverse DCF implies 34.9% earnings growth and the DCF model produces an overvalued reading [E38, E40], but institutional money flow remains decidedly positive with foreign and domestic institutions increasing their holdings, alongside a sector tailwind score of +1.04 in Capital Goods [E35, E36, E37, E65].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months is 42% [E14], and the rules-based screen scores 75 out of 100 [E57]. However, this top-line momentum masks a sharp divergence where compounded profit growth over the same period sits at -9% [E15] and net profit fell -49% year-over-year [E62]. Conceded: relative strength reads 100 against the Nifty 500 and the company is expected to give a good quarter [E44, E52], but this price-led behavior means recently price growth exceeds profit growth by 53%, leaving expectations running far ahead of actual delivery [E50]. Conceded: cash conversion is 2.21x with operating cash flow at Rs 86 Cr [E26, E27], but this did not translate into free cash flow, which plummeted to Rs -12 Cr [E28], driven by expanding debt up to Rs 245 Cr and a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.17x [E30, E32]. Conceded: institutional holdings have increased [E35, E36], yet promoters chose to reduce their stake by 1.50 percentage points down to 42.58% [E34]. Finally, while the Capital Goods sector carries a positive tailwind [E65], it cannot justify a P/E of 134.1x versus a sector benchmark of 23.87x [E6], a negative DCF margin of safety of -490% [E39], and a reverse DCF implying an aggressive 34.9% earnings growth rate [E40].
